w: Robert Tor Russell built this commercial hub in 1929-1933 as the showpiece of Lutyens' Delhi, named for a British royal duke. Renamed Rajiv Chowk in 1995, almost nobody uses the new name - it's still Connaught Place, a shopping magnet that in 2018 ranked the ninth most expensive office spot on the planet.
s: New Delhi's colonial hub that refused its rename
_facts: One of the main financial, commercial and business centres in New Delhi, developed as a showpiece of Lutyens' Delhi
Construction began 1929, completed 1933, designed by Robert Tor Russell, named after Prince Arthur, 1st Duke of Connaught and Strathearn
Officially renamed Rajiv Chowk in 1995, but locals and officials still call it Connaught Place
As of July 2018 ranked the ninth most expensive office location in the world, annual rent $1,650 per square metre
A major shopping, nightlife and tourist destination

w: Every stage of Indian self-government sat inside this Lutyens-and-Baker building at some point: the colonial Imperial Legislative Council from 1927, the Constituent Assembly that wrote the constitution, then independent India's own Parliament for 73 years straight - until a new building took over next door in 2023.
s: 73 years as the seat of Indian democracy
_facts: Seat of the Parliament of India between 26 January 1950 and 18 September 2023, housing the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha for nearly 73 years
Earlier served as the seat of the Imperial Legislative Council (1927-1947) and the Constituent Assembly of India (1947-1950)
Designed by British architects Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker, constructed 1921-1927, opened January 1927
A New Parliament House, built adjacent, was inaugurated 28 May 2023 and replaced this building

w: Edwin Lutyens designed this mansion for Mir Osman Ali Khan, the last Nizam of Hyderabad. Independent India inherited the building and turned it into the Prime Minister's official state guest house, where visiting foreign dignitaries are now hosted for banquets and meetings in rooms built for a princely ruler.
s: A Nizam's mansion, now the PM's state guest house
_facts: Official residence in New Delhi, the State Guest House of the Prime Minister of India
Used by the Government of India for banquets and meetings with visiting foreign dignitaries
Designed by British architect Sir Edwin Lutyens as a residence for Mir Osman Ali Khan, the last Nizam of Hyderabad
